reader.requirement: At --std 85 every KEY IS data-name-2 must be written as a (possibly qualified) data-name with no subscript, on the base name or on a qualifier, even though the key lies within the table; a subscripted (or reference-modified) key operand must be refused.

edition-consulted.switches: edition.SubscriptedClauseOperands (the 2002 subscripted data-name-n reading) is asked only when the caller passes admitsSubscript2002; ClauseDataName passes false, so the condition short-circuits before the edition and every edition takes the refusal arm

reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb885-occurs-key-subscripted; the probes add a subscript on a qualifier, on the subject used as its own key, and the reference-modified form

probes.printed: COBOL2024 'K1 (1)' is written with a subscript; COBOL2024 'K2 OF E2 (1)'; COBOL2024 'E3 (2)' (the subject as key); COBOL2024 'K4 (1:1)' is reference-modified. Identical at --std 2023
unsubscripted keys (including one in an OCCURS DEPENDING ON table) compile and SEARCH ALL runs: AT 4 / E2 OK / E3 OK

reader.notes: The grammar admits a dataReference so the binder can name the fault; ClauseDataName refuses any subscript and registers the operand so no cascade follows. Lead, not a conformance failure: the refusal's closing sentence is ScreenClauseOperandShape's fixed DataBinder.NotSubjectToOccurs ('the operand shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses'), which is false for an OCCURS KEY operand, always subject to the table's OCCURS (the PB1281 caller-states-its-own-rule pattern, not applied to this caller); no kb/Work note names it.

refuter.evidence: rs1.cob (--std 85): COBOL2024 for KEY IS K1 (X1) (indexing by the table's own index-name), K2 (X2 + 1) (relative indexing) and K3 OF E3 (1 2) (two-level subscript on a key of a nested table); the reader's sub1 covered integer subscripts and reference modification. The refusal arm in DataBinder.ClauseDataName passes admitsSubscript2002=false, so no edition arm is taken. cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.5.8.3 SR4  (5.8.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR4.
